title: Managed disks and encryption at host
learningObjective: Add, expand, convert, snapshot and detach managed disks, and choose and configure the right encryption option, especially encryption at host.
foundation: VM disks in Azure are managed disks: Azure handles the underlying storage. Each VM has an OS disk, can have data disks, and often a temporary disk that is wiped on redeployment.
Disk types trade speed for price: Standard HDD, Standard SSD, Premium SSD, Premium SSD v2 and Ultra Disk.

All managed disks are encrypted at rest automatically. Encryption at host goes further: the server running your VM encrypts the temporary disk and disk caches too, so nothing sits unencrypted on that server.
Azure Disk Encryption (ADE), the older option that encrypts inside the operating system, retires on 15 September 2028. Use encryption at host for new VMs.
engineer: Operations: attach or detach data disks while the VM runs; expand disk size (shrinking is not supported; data disks can often be expanded without downtime, then extend the partition in the OS); change disk type (for example Standard SSD → Premium SSD) with the VM deallocated; incremental snapshots for backup or cloning; host caching (None/ReadOnly/ReadWrite) per disk.

Limits: the VM size sets the maximum number of data disks and combined IOPS/throughput; Premium SSD performance depends on disk size (P-tiers) unless you use Premium SSD v2 or Ultra, where IOPS and throughput are set independently. Ultra and Premium SSD v2 have restrictions such as no OS disk support (Ultra) and zone requirements.

Encryption options: server-side encryption (SSE) with platform-managed keys (default, always on); SSE with customer-managed keys through a disk encryption set pointing to a Key Vault key; encryption at host (end-to-end: data is encrypted on the VM host and flows encrypted to Azure Storage); Azure Disk Encryption (legacy, inside the guest).

Encryption at host: the temporary disk and ephemeral OS disk are encrypted with platform-managed keys; OS and data disk caches use platform- or customer-managed keys, matching each disk's encryption type (use a disk encryption set for customer-managed keys).

Turning it on: register the EncryptionAtHost feature on the subscription once (az feature register --namespace Microsoft.Compute --name EncryptionAtHost, wait for Registered); pick a supported VM size (older sizes are not supported; the SKU capability is EncryptionAtHostSupported). New VM: portal Disks tab > Encryption at host. Existing VM: deallocate it, set VM > Disks > Additional settings > Encryption at host, save, start. Scale sets: only VMs created after enabling it are encrypted.

Azure Disk Encryption (ADE) uses BitLocker (Windows) or DM-Crypt (Linux) inside the guest, with keys in a Key Vault in the same region and subscription. It retires on 15 September 2028; after that, ADE disks fail to unlock on reboot. Encryption at host cannot be enabled on a VM that has, or ever had, ADE, so migration means new disks on a new VM.
Confidential disk encryption is available for confidential VMs.

animation.caption: Open 'Resize, disks and encryption': try disk operations and turn on encryption at host.

example.title: Expanding a full data disk
body: A database VM's 128 GiB data disk is 95% full. The admin expands it to 256 GiB in the portal while the VM runs, then extends the volume in Disk Management.

Security then asks that the temporary disk and caches are encrypted too. The admin registers EncryptionAtHost, deallocates the VM, turns on Encryption at host under Disks > Additional settings, and starts it again.

prerequisites: Supported VM size for the disk type
Encryption at host: EncryptionAtHost feature registered, a supported VM size, and no Azure Disk Encryption on the VM now or before
permissions: Virtual Machine Contributor for disk and VM operations
Key Vault key access for the disk encryption set's managed identity (customer-managed keys)
limits: Max data disks depends on VM size
Encryption at host on an existing VM requires deallocation
Encryption at host is blocked on VMs that ever had ADE
portal: VM > Disks > + Create and attach a new disk / Attach existing; Detach.
Disk > Size + performance: increase size or change tier.
Disk > Encryption: choose encryption type and disk encryption set.
Create a VM > Disks tab > Encryption at host.
Existing VM: Stop (deallocate) > Disks > Additional settings > Encryption at host = Yes > Save > Start.
configuration.cli:
az vm disk attach -g rg-app --vm-name vm1 --name vm1-data1 --new --size-gb 128 --sku Premium_LRS
az disk update -g rg-app -n vm1-data1 --size-gb 256
az vm deallocate -g rg-app -n vm1 && az disk update -g rg-app -n vm1-data1 --sku Premium_LRS
az snapshot create -g rg-app -n vm1-data1-snap --source vm1-data1 --incremental true
az feature register --namespace Microsoft.Compute --name EncryptionAtHost
az feature show --namespace Microsoft.Compute --name EncryptionAtHost --query properties.state
az vm create -g rg-app -n vm2 --image Ubuntu2204 --size Standard_D2s_v5 --encryption-at-host --generate-ssh-keys
az vm deallocate -g rg-app -n vm1
az vm update -g rg-app -n vm1 --set securityProfile.encryptionAtHost=true
az vm start -g rg-app -n vm1
configuration.powershell:
$vm = Get-AzVM -ResourceGroupName rg-app -Name vm1
$cfg = New-AzDiskConfig -Location westeurope -CreateOption Empty -DiskSizeGB 128 -SkuName Premium_LRS
$disk = New-AzDisk -ResourceGroupName rg-app -DiskName vm1-data1 -Disk $cfg
Add-AzVMDataDisk -VM $vm -Name vm1-data1 -CreateOption Attach -ManagedDiskId $disk.Id -Lun 0 | Update-AzVM
Register-AzProviderFeature -FeatureName EncryptionAtHost -ProviderNamespace Microsoft.Compute
Stop-AzVM -ResourceGroupName rg-app -Name vm1 -Force
$vm = Get-AzVM -ResourceGroupName rg-app -Name vm1
Update-AzVM -ResourceGroupName rg-app -VM $vm -EncryptionAtHost $true
Start-AzVM -ResourceGroupName rg-app -Name vm1

lab.objective: Predict which disk operations need downtime and which encryption prerequisites are missing.
steps: Try each disk operation, with the VM running and deallocated.
Select Encryption at host and fix each blocker: feature registration, VM size, deallocation.
Tick 'ever had Azure Disk Encryption' and see why migration needs a new VM.
expected: Shrinking is blocked; type change needs deallocation

validation.text: Turned on encryption at host successfully

failureScenarios: Enabling encryption at host while the VM runs
Too many data disks for the size
lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.fix: Create a smaller disk and copy data.

troubleshooting.symptom: Encryption at host option is greyed out or fails.
troubleshooting.cause: Feature not registered, VM size not supported, VM still running, or the VM had Azure Disk Encryption.
troubleshooting.fix: Register EncryptionAtHost, resize to a supported size, deallocate; for ex-ADE VMs migrate to a new VM.

troubleshooting.symptom: New disk size not visible in the OS.
troubleshooting.fix: Extend the volume (Disk Management / growpart and resize2fs).
Resize the VM to one with more data disk slots.

comparisons.difference: Block volumes similar to managed disks; gp3/io2 correspond to Premium SSD v2/Ultra-like provisioning.
Shared SMB/NFS file storage rather than a block device.

misconceptions.myth: Disks are unencrypted unless you turn on extra encryption.
misconceptions.reality: SSE with platform-managed keys is always on; encryption at host adds the temp disk and caches.

misconceptions.myth: You can switch an ADE VM to encryption at host in place.
misconceptions.reality: Not allowed on a VM that ever had ADE; create a new VM with new disks.

misconceptions.myth: You can switch a disk to Premium while the VM runs.
misconceptions.reality: Disk type changes need the VM deallocated.

architectureDecisions: Use Premium SSD (or v2) for production databases.
Use encryption at host for new VMs (add a disk encryption set if you need your own keys); plan ADE migrations before 15 Sep 2028.

walkthrough.subtitle: Give a VM the right disks, change them safely, and turn on encryption at host.
learn: Encryption: always-on SSE, your own keys, encryption at host

steps.label: Disks
steps.title: The database needs more space and faster disks
body: And the auditor asks how the disks are encrypted, and who controls the keys.

steps.label: Disk roles
steps.title: Three kinds of disk on a VM
body: OS disk: the operating system. Temporary disk: fast local scratch space, lost when the VM is deallocated or moved to other hardware. Data disks: your data, attached as needed (the number depends on VM size).

callout.text: Never keep important data on the temporary disk.

steps.label: Types
steps.title: Disk types, from cheap to fast
body: Standard HDD, Standard SSD, Premium SSD, Premium SSD v2 and Ultra Disk. Bigger Premium disks get more IOPS and throughput. You can change the type when the VM is deallocated (with some limits for v2 and Ultra).

steps.label: Operations
steps.title: Everyday disk jobs
body: Attach or detach data disks (often without a restart). Increase size (never shrink), then extend the partition inside the OS. Take a snapshot for a quick copy; create new disks from it.

steps.label: Encryption
steps.title: Encryption, layer by layer
body: Server-side encryption (SSE) is always on: every managed disk is encrypted in storage with a Microsoft key. Want your own key? Create a disk encryption set that points to a Key Vault key.
Encryption at host goes one step further: the server running your VM encrypts the temporary disk and disk caches, so data is encrypted before it even leaves the server.

callout.text: Azure Disk Encryption (ADE), the older in-OS option, retires on 15 Sep 2028. Use encryption at host instead.

steps.label: Host encryption
steps.title: Turning on encryption at host
body:
1. Register the EncryptionAtHost feature on the subscription (once).
2. Use a VM size that supports it.
3. New VM: tick Encryption at host on the Disks tab. Existing VM: stop (deallocate) it, then Disks > Additional settings > Encryption at host > Yes.

callout.text: A VM that has, or ever had, ADE can never get encryption at host. Migrate to a new VM with new disks.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Disks
body: Right disk, right size, right keys.
recap: HDD < Standard SSD < Premium SSD < Premium v2 / Ultra
SSE always on; CMK via disk encryption set
Encryption at host: register feature, supported size, deallocate
ADE retires 15 Sep 2028; ex-ADE VMs need a new VM

handsOn.title: Add, resize and snapshot a data disk, and turn on encryption at host
handsOn.cost: Low. A B1s Linux VM costs about US$0.01 per hour (it is in the free account's 750 free hours). Delete it the same day. A small data disk and snapshot add cents.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.

Create a small Linux VM: Virtual machines > + Create > Azure virtual machine. Resource group rg-az104-lab, name vm-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you), image Ubuntu Server 24.04 LTS, size Standard_B1s, authentication: password, username azureuser. Inbound ports: None. Review + create > Create. If the VM cannot reach the internet later, its subnet is private (the default for new networks): open the virtual network > Subnets, untick 'Enable private subnet', save, then stop and start the VM. In production use a NAT gateway instead.

steps.do: Open vm-lab > Settings > Disks > + Create and attach a new disk. Name: vm-lab-data1, Standard SSD, size 4 GiB. Apply.
steps.see: The data disk listed under Data disks with LUN 0.

steps.do: Stop (deallocate) the VM. Open the data disk > Settings > Size + performance. Choose 8 GiB. Save.
steps.see: The disk now shows 8 GiB. Shrinking is not offered.

steps.do: On the same disk, try changing the performance tier or disk type to Premium SSD.
steps.see: Allowed while the VM is deallocated. Change it back to Standard SSD.

steps.do: Open the data disk > Overview > Create snapshot. Name: snap-data1, type: Incremental.
steps.see: A snapshot resource in the group.

steps.do: Open the data disk > Settings > Encryption.
steps.see: Encryption at rest with a platform-managed key; options for customer-managed keys via a disk encryption set.

steps.do: Open Cloud Shell (Bash) and register the encryption-at-host feature. Repeat the second command until it says Registered (a few minutes).
steps.code:
az feature register --namespace Microsoft.Compute --name EncryptionAtHost
az feature show --namespace Microsoft.Compute --name EncryptionAtHost --query properties.state -o tsv
az provider register --namespace Microsoft.Compute
# Does your VM size support it? (use your VM's region; True = supported)
az vm list-skus -l uaenorth --size Standard_B1s --query "[0].capabilities[?name=='EncryptionAtHostSupported'].value" -o tsv

steps.do: With vm-lab still stopped (deallocated), open vm-lab > Settings > Disks > Additional settings. Set Encryption at host to Yes. Save.
steps.see: The save succeeds. If the option is greyed out, the VM size does not support it (resize to a D-series v5 size) or the feature is not registered yet.
steps.tip: It only saves while the VM is deallocated.

steps.do: Start vm-lab. In Cloud Shell, check the setting.
steps.code: az vm show -g rg-az104-lab -n vm-lab --query securityProfile.encryptionAtHost

steps.do: Back on Disks, detach the data disk and Save.
steps.see: The disk still exists in the resource group, unattached (and still billed).

check: You grew a disk and made an incremental snapshot.
az vm show reports encryptionAtHost true.
cleanup: When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
